en: Giotto was Europe's pillar of the Halley armada — a spin-stabilised 960 kg probe wrapped in a layered Whipple-Kevlar dust shield. A dust impact ~7.6 seconds before closest approach destabilised the spin axis and killed the camera, but the other instruments kept transmitting through the coma. After hibernating in heliocentric orbit, Giotto reactivated 1990 + used Earth gravity assist to retarget to comet 26P/Grigg-Skjellerup, flying past it at 200 km on 1992-07-10 — the closest cometary flyby ever performed.

en: ESA's flagship comet-rendezvous mission. en: Hera is the European Space Agency's contribution to humanity's first planetary-defence experiment. In 2022 NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos — the small moon of the asteroid Didymos — and measurably shortened its orbit. Hera, launched in October 2024 on a Falcon 9, is flying to the same binary asteroid (with a 2025 Mars gravity assist en route) to conduct the detailed post-impact survey DART couldn't: the size of the crater, Dimorphos's mass and internal structure, and precisely how much momentum the impact transferred. en: DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) was the first planetary-defense mission ever flown — a 611-kg spacecraft sent to hit a 160-m asteroid hard enough to change its orbit. Launched 2021-11-24 on a Falcon 9; the SMART Nav autonomous navigation system took over 4 hours before impact to distinguish Dimorphos from its parent and target the smaller body. Impact 2022-09-26 at 23:14 UTC at ~6.6 km/s. Measured orbital-period change: 33 minutes (4.2%), exceeding the 73-second success threshold by ~25×. Momentum-transfer enhancement factor β ≈ 3.6 indicated significant carry from ejected surface material. en: Apollo 1 was the planned first crewed flight of the Apollo Block I CSM, originally designated AS-204 and scheduled to launch 1967-02-21 from LC-34. During a routine "plugs-out" test on 1967-01-27 17:31 EST, with the crew sealed inside the pressurised pure-oxygen cabin, a flash fire ignited in the lower-equipment bay — likely a Teflon-insulated wire arc through silver-plated copper that had been damaged during installation. Cabin pressure spiked to 29 psi within 15 seconds; the inward-opening hatch couldn't be unsealed against the pressure differential. Gus Grissom, Ed White, and Roger Chaffee died from asphyxiation within seconds. The investigation led to a complete Block I → Block II redesign + the safer outward-opening unified hatch + non-flammable cabin materials + pre-launch nitrogen-rich cabin atmosphere. Apollo 1's official designation was assigned posthumously to honour the crew. Subsequent Apollo missions (CSM-101 through CSM-114) flew the Block II hardware that this redesign produced.

It was the final item on the Gemini checklist, and with it the program closed, having taught NASA everything the Moon would require.

en: Gemini 4 is remembered for one photograph: Ed White, tethered to the spacecraft by a gold umbilical, floating over a blue Earth with a handheld maneuvering gun — the first American to walk in space. The moment was so exhilarating that when Mission Control ordered him back inside after twenty minutes, White called it the saddest moment of his life. en: After two flights that ended in scares, Sigma 7 was the one that was boring on purpose — and that was the achievement. Wally Schirra called it a textbook engineering test and flew it like one: minimal experiments, careful conservation of every kilogram of fuel and every amp of power, six orbits spent proving the spacecraft could be operated with discipline rather than wrestled. He splashed down almost on top of the recovery carrier. In a program that had been improvising under pressure, Sigma 7 showed the Americans had learned to fly the thing calmly — the prerequisite for the far longer missions ahead.
cur: दो उड़ानों के बाद जो डर के साथ समाप्त हुई थीं, Sigma 7 वह था जो जानबूझकर नीरस था — और वह ही उपलब्धि थी। वॉली शिरा ने इसे एक पाठ्यपुस्तक इंजीनियरिंग परीक्षण कहा और उसे उसी तरह उड़ाया: न्यूनतम प्रयोग, ईंधन के प्रत्येक किलोग्राम और शक्ति के प्रत्येक एम्पियर के सावधान संरक्षण, छह कक्षाएँ यह साबित करने में बिताई गईं कि अंतरिक्ष यान को अनुशासन के साथ संचालित किया जा सकता है न कि संघर्ष के साथ। वह लगभग पुनरुद्धार वाहक के ठीक ऊपर छींटे मारे गए। एक कार्यक्रम में जो दबाव में सुधार कर रहा था, Sigma 7 ने दिखाया कि अमेरिकियों ने चीज़ को शांति से उड़ाना सीख लिया था — लंबी उड़ानों के लिए पूर्वापेक्षा।

en: Wally Schirra's 6-orbit flight — doubled Glenn's and Carpenter's mission length. Schirra called his flight a "textbook engineering test" — minimal experimental load, focus on conserving consumables, validating the vehicle for longer duration. Flight duration 9 h 13 min; orbital parameters 161 × 283 km. Splashed down ~445 km NE of Midway in the Pacific — first Mercury flight to splash in the Pacific. Aurora 7 had used 38 kg of attitude control gas; Schirra used only 32 kg with double the flight time. Capsule Sigma 7 on display at the Astronaut Memorial Planetarium and Observatory, Cocoa FL.
cur: वॉली शिरा की 6-कक्षा उड़ान — ग्लेन और कार्पेंटर की मिशन अवधि को दोगुना किया। शिरा ने अपनी उड़ान को "पाठ्यपुस्तक इंजीनियरिंग परीक्षण" कहा — न्यूनतम प्रायोगिक भार, खपत योग्य पदार्थों के संरक्षण पर ध्यान केंद्रित, लंबी अवधि के लिए वाहन की पुष्टि। उड़ान अवधि 9 घंटे 13 मिनट; कक्षीय पैरामीटर 161 × 283 किमी। मिडवे के उत्तर-पूर्व में प्रशांत महासागर में ~445 किमी में छींटे मारे गए — प्रशांत महासागर में पहली Mercury उड़ान। Aurora 7 ने मुद्रा नियंत्रण गैस के 38 किग्रा का उपयोग किया; शिरा ने केवल 32 किग्रा का उपयोग दोगुनी उड़ान के समय के साथ किया। कैप्सूल Sigma 7 Astronaut Memorial Planetarium and Observatory, Cocoa FL में प्रदर्शन पर है।

en: Skylab 2 is the mission that saved America's first space station and, in doing so, proved that astronauts are repair crews as much as explorers. Skylab had reached orbit crippled — its sun shield ripped off during launch, one solar panel gone, the other jammed shut, the interior overheating toward uninhabitable. Pete Conrad's crew flew up to a station that might have been a write-off, deployed a parasol sunshade through a small airlock to cool it, and then freed the stuck panel in a dangerous, improvised spacewalk that restored its power. It was the first time a crew had rescued a failing spacecraft in orbit, and it rewrote the assumption that space hardware was disposable.
cur: Skylab 2 वह मिशन है जिसने अमेरिका के पहले अंतरिक्ष स्टेशन को बचाया और ऐसा करते हुए यह साबित किया कि अंतरिक्ष यात्री खोजकर्ताओं जितने ही मरम्मत दल भी हैं। Skylab क्षतिग्रस्त अवस्था में कक्षा में पहुंचा था — प्रक्षेपण के दौरान इसकी सूर्य ढाल फट गई थी, एक सौर पैनल गायब हो गया था, दूसरा जाम होकर बंद था, और आंतरिक भाग अत्यधिक गर्मी से निर्जन होने की ओर बढ़ रहा था। पीट कॉनराड के दल ने एक ऐसे स्टेशन की ओर उड़ान भरी जो शायद बट्टे खाते में जाने वाला था, इसे ठंडा करने के लिए एक छोटे एयरलॉक के माध्यम से एक पैरासोल सनशेड तैनात किया, और फिर एक खतरनाक, तात्कालिक स्पेसवॉक में फंसे हुए पैनल को मुक्त किया जिसने इसकी शक्ति बहाल की। यह पहली बार था जब किसी दल ने कक्षा में विफल हो रहे अंतरिक्ष यान को बचाया था, और इसने यह धारणा बदल दी कि अंतरिक्ष उपकरण डिस्पोजेबल हैं।

en: Conrad, Kerwin and Weitz — the first crew to inhabit the US Skylab space station. Launched 1973-05-25 13:00 UTC on Saturn IB (SA-206), 11 days after Skylab itself was damaged at launch (the micrometeoroid / sun shield ripped off, taking one solar wing with it and jamming the second). The crew executed a 28-day rescue: Weitz attempted (and failed) to free the jammed wing during a 38-minute stand-up EVA on day 1, then Conrad and Kerwin successfully cut the restraining strap on a 3.5-hour EVA on day 14, restoring power. en: Korolev's polished aluminium sphere — 58 cm wide, 83.6 kg, two transmitters on 20.005 and 40.002 MHz — became the first human-made object to reach orbit on 1957-10-04 19:28 UTC. The flight was an OKB-1 side project: Korolev needed a lightweight payload for his still-developmental R-7 ICBM and pitched 'PS-1' (Prosteyshiy Sputnik — 'simplest satellite') to Khrushchev as a propaganda coup. Sputnik 1 also returned the first orbital ionospheric and atmospheric-density data — engineers used the Doppler shift on the 20 / 40 MHz carriers to map air density at 215 km, work that fed into every subsequent re-entry calculation.

en: Vostok 3 opened the first act of a piece of orbital theatre. A day after Andriyan Nikolayev reached orbit, Vostok 4 followed him up, and for a while the two spacecraft flew within a few kilometres of each other — the first time two crewed craft had ever been in space together. To the world it looked like a rendezvous, and the Soviets were glad to let it. In truth neither ship could maneuver; the closeness came from launching one almost into the other's path, and the gap widened steadily after. A genuine first and a bit of a magic trick at once — and a hint at the real skill, true rendezvous, that no one yet had.
cur: Vostok 3 ने कक्षीय रंगमंच के पहले अधिनियम को खोला। आंद्रियान निकोलायेव की कक्षा तक पहुँचने के एक दिन बाद, Vostok 4 उनके पीछे चला गया, और कुछ समय के लिए दोनों अंतरिक्ष यान एक-दूसरे के कुछ किलोमीटर के भीतर उड़े — पहली बार दो क्रूयुक्त विमान कभी एक साथ अंतरिक्ष में थे। दुनिया के लिए यह एक रेंडेज़्वस जैसा लगता था, और सोवियतों को इसे होने देने में खुशी थी। सच में न तो कोई जहाज युक्तिसंगत कर सकता था; निकटता एक को लगभग दूसरे के पथ में लॉन्च करने से आई, और अंतराल शुरुआत के बाद लगातार चौड़ा होता गया। एक असली पहला और एक जादुई चाल एक साथ — और वास्तविक कौशल, सच्ची रेंडेज़्वस का एक संकेत, जो अभी तक किसी के पास नहीं था।

The simultaneous flight was a propaganda response to US suborbital missions and to John Glenn's Friendship 7. Nikolayev landed 1962-08-15 06:52 UTC near Karaganda, Kazakh SSR, after almost 4 days in space.

en: Vostok 4 was the answer to Vostok 3 — the second ship in the first dual flight, and the moment two humans in two separate spacecraft first spoke to each other in orbit. Pavel Popovich launched a day after Nikolayev and closed to within about six and a half kilometres, near enough to trade radio voice directly, ship to ship, rather than through the ground. Like its partner it couldn't maneuver to hold the distance, so the two drifted apart. But the image of two cosmonauts circling the Earth in formation, talking to each other, was exactly the kind of first the program was built to manufacture.
cur: Vostok 4 Vostok 3 का उत्तर था — पहली द्वि-उड़ान में दूसरा जहाज़, और वह क्षण जब दो इंसान दो अलग-अलग अंतरिक्ष यानों में पहली बार कक्षा में एक-दूसरे से बात करते हैं। पावेल पोपोविच निकोलायेव के एक दिन बाद प्रक्षेपित हुए और लगभग साढ़े छह किलोमीटर के भीतर आ गए, इतना पास कि रेडियो आवाज़ सीधे जहाज़ से जहाज़ तक आदान-प्रदान कर सकते थे, जमीन के माध्यम से नहीं। अपने साथी की तरह, यह दूरी को बनाए रखने के लिए पैंतरेबाज़ी नहीं कर सकता था, इसलिए दोनों अलग हो गए। लेकिन पृथ्वी के चारों ओर गठन में घूमते हुए दो कॉस्मोनॉट्स की छवि, एक-दूसरे से बात करते हुए, बिल्कुल वही तरह का पहला कदम था जो कार्यक्रम निर्मित करने के लिए बनाया गया था।

en: Pavel Popovich's 48-orbit flight, launched 1962-08-12 08:02 UTC, twenty-four hours after Vostok 3. The two capsules came within ~6.5 km and exchanged the first voice radio communications between cosmonauts in orbit. Popovich was ordered down a day early when ground controllers misinterpreted a coded phrase about thunder as the duress code-word for early termination — the real signal was a routine weather observation. Landed 1962-08-15 06:59 UTC near Karaganda, seven minutes after Vostok 3.

en: Vostok 5 set a record that still stands. Valery Bykovsky flew nearly five days alone in orbit — eighty-one laps of the planet — which remains, six decades on, the longest solo spaceflight anyone has ever made. It was an endurance test above all, pushing a single cosmonaut and a small spacecraft far past the day Titov managed, to see whether a person could simply keep going. He could. And Bykovsky wasn't even the headline of his own mission: two days into his flight, Vostok 6 went up carrying the first woman in space, and the world's attention went with her.
